Answer: D
Reason: The imaging series demonstrates a rapid progression from initial interstitial opacities to severe bilateral alveolar consolidations (Figure 4), followed by complete radiological resolution in the follow-up images (Figures 5a and 5b). This pattern of fulminant pulmonary involvement with subsequent full recovery is characteristic of Weil Syndrome (severe leptospirosis) in this context, distinguishing it from conditions like Goodpasture syndrome or crack lung which typically have different outcomes or histories.
